newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields lower,still need RBA to act.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields lower,still need RBA to act.

text.p: *Australian bond yields start lower, largely reflecting a rally in the U.S. on Monday, but interest stays light as the market marks time awaiting a widely-expected policy easing.
*A$500 million T-bond tender result due 2.00 p.m. (0400 GMT).
Australian bond yields started lower, largely reflecting a rally in the U.S. on Monday, but interest remained light as the market continued to mark time awaiting a widely expected policy easing.

"For now we will be watching what the U.S. does and acting accordingly, but the main event for us remains next Wednesday," one trader said referring to August 6, the day after the Reserve Bank board meeting where a rate cut is expected to be endorsed.
A 50 basis point easing in current 5.5 percent official rates remains factored in, limiting scope for rallies in the interim period.

Today's local Treasury bond tender may give the market some self-generated direction later today, but at A$500 million traders saw few problems absorbing the stock given the shortages of stock across the curve after the recent strong rally.
Final bids for the two stocks on offer, the October 2007 and and the September 2009, are due in at 12.45 p.m. (0245 GMT) and the result will be announced at 2.00 p.m. (0400 GMT).
U.S. Treasuries rallied after the Treasury department said that it expected a net market borrowing requirement for the third quarter of US$10 billion, about half of what U.S. analysts had expected.

The local market slightly underperformed the U.S., where the market is also anticipating a favourable outcome to the second quarter U.S. employment costs index later Tuesday. New Zealand debt again performed weakly as the market attempted to counter sustained weakness in the N.Z. dollar.
